title: Three-tier Synthetic Arbiter AI: Tier I claims random/adjacent sectors; Tier II detects and blocks any collinear vector where the opponent holds 2 of 3 sectors; Tier III executes full recursive Minimax lookahead (prioritizing immediate winning triads, blocking opponent threats, seizing the central nexus or corner anchors, and setting up dual-vector forks).
author_role: Principal Systems & Economy Architect (Data schemas, progression curves, state ledgers)
summary: Three-tier Synthetic Arbiter decision engine handling heuristic randoms, tactical 2-in-a-row counter-blocks, and zero-sum Minimax lookahead.
technical_specification: Represent sectors as `state.grid[0..8]`. When `state.activeContender === 2` and `!state.roundOver`: if `tier === 1`, filter vacant sectors, prioritize adjacent open cells with 40% random noise. If `tier === 2`, search canonical triads `TRIADS = [[0,1,2],[3,4,5],[6,7,8],[0,3,6],[1,4,7],[2,5,8],[0,4,8],[2,4,6]]`; if Arbiter has 2/3 claim third (win), else if Player has 2/3 claim third (block), else fallback to center `4` then corners `[0,2,6,8]`. If `tier === 3`, run depth-limited minimax (`score = +10 - depth` for Arbiter win, `-10 + depth` for Player win, 0 for draw) to select optimum index. Queue sector inscription at `state.aiMoveIndex` with a 350ms kinetic deliberate delay.
acceptance_criteria: Tier I plays valid vacant sectors without locking or throwing runtime errors.
Tier II consistently takes immediate wins and blocks opponent two-in-a-row threats.
Tier III never loses an opening or reactive game across standard tic-tac-toe permutations.
